analysis:
Examined ClusterService.swift head lines 473–1339: relay scope and shared-token handling, paired commands, cache-settings synchronization, owned-process stopping, update replanning, coordinator approval refresh, supervision acknowledgements and restart accounting. The complete range map identifies only lines 1131–1133 and comments at 1301–1302 as changes within these units; the surrounding relay, command authorization and process-custody logic is not evidence of a new regression.
At 1131–1133, approval set-aside recording now delegates to ClusterApprovalCheck.setAside(by:worker:now:) and includes the saved worker digest. The result.changed guard and clearing on successful .save remain visible. This interacts with approval lifetime checks at 1072–1080, local fallback/restart at 1109–1127, and worker-update replanning at 965–1013. No independently supported vulnerability is established here, but integration must inspect the helper and its consumers to verify that retained approvals cannot regain coordinator-serving authority after expiry, revocation or a worker change (A-016, A-017, T-052, T-053, T-054). The comment change at 1301–1302 does not itself alter quick-end accounting.
Also reconcile the new environment injection listed in the file-change context with partEnvironment and child startup in other units, particularly cache kill-switch preservation (T-041) and worker identity. Those implementations and the rest of the changed startup lines are outside this supplied source scope; their absence is a coverage limit, not proof of missing controls.
